lines.text: Nine squares, three colors, and the center one is already red.
lines.caption: Nine squares, three colors, and the center one is already red.

lines.text: Neighbors can't match. <short pause> How many ways can we color the rest?
lines.caption: Neighbors can't match. How many ways can we color the rest?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count them together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count them together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Each square of this three by three grid is colored red, blue or green.
lines.caption: Each square of this three by three grid is colored red, blue or green.

lines.text: The center square is red. Squares that share a side must be different colors.
lines.caption: The center square is red. Squares that share a side must be different colors.

lines.text: Not every color has to be used. How many colorings are there?
lines.caption: Not every color has to be used. How many colorings are there?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Four squares share a side with the center. Let's call them the edge squares.
lines.caption: Four squares share a side with the center. Let's call them the edge squares.

lines.text: The other four are the corners. Each corner touches two edge squares, but NOT the center.
lines.caption: The other four are the corners. Each corner touches two edge squares, but NOT the center.

lines.text: We need to count every way to color these eight squares.
lines.caption: We need to count every way to color these eight squares.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's color the edge squares first. Each one touches red, so it's blue or green.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's color the edge squares first. Each one touches red, so it's blue or green.

lines.text: Two choices, four times. Two times two times two times two is sixteen edge patterns.
lines.caption: Two choices, four times. Two times two times two times two is sixteen edge patterns.

lines.text: Now look at one corner. Say its two edge neighbors are both blue.
lines.caption: Now look at one corner. Say its two edge neighbors are both blue.

lines.text: It can't be blue. Red is fine, since it doesn't touch the center. So red or green: two options.
lines.caption: It can't be blue. Red is fine, since it doesn't touch the center. So red or green: two options.

lines.text: Now say its neighbors are blue and green. Both are out, so the corner must be red. Just one option.
lines.caption: Now say its neighbors are blue and green. Both are out, so the corner must be red. Just one option.

lines.text: So a corner has two options when its neighbors match, and one when they don't.
lines.caption: So a corner has two options when its neighbors match, and one when they don't.

lines.text: Let's sort the sixteen edge patterns by how many corners get two options.
lines.caption: Let's sort the sixteen edge patterns by how many corners get two options.

lines.text: First, all four edges match: all blue, or all green. That's two patterns.
lines.caption: First, all four edges match: all blue, or all green. That's two patterns.

lines.text: Every corner gets two options: sixteen colorings each. Two times sixteen is thirty-two.
lines.caption: Every corner gets two options: sixteen colorings each. Two times sixteen is thirty-two.

lines.text: Next, the colors take turns around the ring, like a checkerboard. Again, two patterns.
lines.caption: Next, the colors take turns around the ring, like a checkerboard. Again, two patterns.

lines.text: No corner has matching neighbors, so all four corners are red. One coloring each, so that's two.
lines.caption: No corner has matching neighbors, so all four corners are red. One coloring each, so that's two.

lines.text: That leaves twelve patterns. Eight split three and one. Four split two and two, side by side.
lines.caption: That leaves twelve patterns. Eight split three and one. Four split two and two, side by side.

lines.text: Either way, exactly two corners have matching neighbors. So each gives two times two, which is four.
lines.caption: Either way, exactly two corners have matching neighbors. So each gives two times two, which is four.

lines.text: Twelve patterns times four is forty-eight.
lines.caption: Twelve patterns times four is forty-eight.

lines.text: Thirty-two, plus forty-eight, plus two, is eighty-two! The answer is D.
lines.caption: Thirty-two, plus forty-eight, plus two, is eighty-two! The answer is D.

lines.text: Here's a second way. Let's sort colorings by how many corners are NOT red.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Let's sort colorings by how many corners are NOT red.

lines.text: A red corner is always safe, because edge squares are never red.
lines.caption: A red corner is always safe, because edge squares are never red.

lines.text: A corner that isn't red needs matching neighbors. If they're both blue, it must be green.
lines.caption: A corner that isn't red needs matching neighbors. If they're both blue, it must be green.

lines.text: No non-red corners: every corner is red, and the edges are free. That's sixteen.
lines.caption: No non-red corners: every corner is red, and the edges are free. That's sixteen.

lines.text: One non-red corner: four to pick. Its two neighbors match: two ways.
lines.caption: One non-red corner: four to pick. Its two neighbors match: two ways.

lines.text: The other two edges are free: four ways. Four times two times four is thirty-two.
lines.caption: The other two edges are free: four ways. Four times two times four is thirty-two.

lines.text: Two on the same side: four pairs. Three edges match, one is free: four ways each. That's sixteen.
lines.caption: Two on the same side: four pairs. Three edges match, one is free: four ways each. That's sixteen.

lines.text: Two opposite corners: two pairs. Each needs its own matching edges: four ways each. That's eight.
lines.caption: Two opposite corners: two pairs. Each needs its own matching edges: four ways each. That's eight.

lines.text: Three non-red corners: four to pick, and all edges match. That's eight. All four non-red: two.
lines.caption: Three non-red corners: four to pick, and all edges match. That's eight. All four non-red: two.

lines.text: Sixteen plus thirty-two plus sixteen plus eight plus eight plus two is eighty-two. It matches!
lines.caption: Sixteen plus thirty-two plus sixteen plus eight plus eight plus two is eighty-two. It matches!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? Edges first is quicker. This way is a great double-check.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? Edges first is quicker. This way is a great double-check.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Sixteen counts only the edge patterns. It forgets to color the corners.
lines.caption: Sixteen counts only the edge patterns. It forgets to color the corners.

lines.text: Thirty-two is what you'd get if you only kept the patterns where all four edges match.
lines.caption: Thirty-two is what you'd get if you only kept the patterns where all four edges match.

lines.text: Eighty-one is three to the fourth, a tempting guess. Or what you'd get if you missed one coloring.
lines.caption: Eighty-one is three to the fourth, a tempting guess. Or what you'd get if you missed one coloring.

lines.text: One hundred sixty-two is what you'd get if you doubled eighty-one. That's far too many.
lines.caption: One hundred sixty-two is what you'd get if you doubled eighty-one. That's far too many.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. When choices depend on the neighbors, split into cases and count each one.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. When choices depend on the neighbors, split into cases and count each one.

scenes.chapter: Your turn: a two by three grid

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a two by three grid, with the same three colors.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a two by three grid, with the same three colors.

lines.text: The middle of the bottom row is red, and neighbors must differ. How many colorings are there?
lines.caption: The middle of the bottom row is red, and neighbors must differ. How many colorings are there?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.chapter: Two by three grid: the answer

lines.text: Let's check. Three squares touch the red one: bottom left, bottom right, and top middle.
lines.caption: Let's check. Three squares touch the red one: bottom left, bottom right, and top middle.

lines.text: Each is blue or green. Two times two times two is eight patterns.
lines.caption: Each is blue or green. Two times two times two is eight patterns.

lines.text: Each top corner touches the top middle square and one bottom square.
lines.caption: Each top corner touches the top middle square and one bottom square.

lines.text: If all three match: two patterns, with two times two, four colorings each. That's eight.
lines.caption: If all three match: two patterns, with two times two, four colorings each. That's eight.

lines.text: If just one bottom square matches the top middle: four patterns, two colorings each. That's eight.
lines.caption: If just one bottom square matches the top middle: four patterns, two colorings each. That's eight.

lines.text: If neither matches: two patterns, with one coloring each. That's two.
lines.caption: If neither matches: two patterns, with one coloring each. That's two.

lines.text: Eight plus eight plus two is eighteen! If you found eighteen, amazing work!
lines.caption: Eight plus eight plus two is eighteen! If you found eighteen, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Color the squares next to the red center first. Each one is blue or green.
lines.caption: Color the squares next to the red center first. Each one is blue or green.

lines.text: Then a corner gets two options when its neighbors match, and just one when they don't.
lines.caption: Then a corner gets two options when its neighbors match, and just one when they don't.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
